definitions.explanation: The Japanese period mark (。) placed at the end of a sentence. One of the basic punctuation marks in Japanese writing.

examples.japanese: {文|ぶん}の{終|お}わりに{句点|くてん}を{打|う}つ。
examples.english: Place a period at the end of a sentence.

examples.japanese: {句点|くてん}と{読点|とうてん}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I learned how to use periods and commas.

examples.japanese: メッセージアプリでは{句点|くてん}を{付|つ}けない{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More and more people don't use periods in messaging apps.

notes: The Japanese period is 。(a small circle), not a dot like in English. Common collocations: {句点|くてん}を{打|う}つ (to put a period), {句点|くてん}を{付|つ}ける (to add a period). The pair of {句点|くてん} (period) and {読点|とうてん} (comma、) are together called {句読点|くとうてん} (punctuation marks). In modern messaging, younger Japanese speakers often omit {句点|くてん} in casual texts, as ending with 。 can feel cold or distant.
